text:
joel: Quick product sync 1 min: we need a clear scoping doc for routing lanes + multi-region + tenant isolation. Sales is pushing for firm SLAs.

nick: Agree. Can we make a prioritized spec that maps to deals? Small ask: include which features we can ship in <90d vs 90-270d vs >270d.

sana: My rough split: short (<90d): policy routing primitives (latency, geo, cost), per-tenant hints, and a minimal affinity cookie. medium (90-270d): reserved pools, tenant lanes, quarantine flow, and required runbooks. long (>270d): DSL, active-active, encrypted KV replication, eviction semantics.

meera: Ops note: for medium-phase we must define runbook triggers and an automated fallback path. Otherwise SRE won't sign off.

keiko: For production: add a routing SLI that measures cross-region routing latency and misrouting rate. Suggest misroute threshold <=0.5% per day for launch.

eva: Sales asks (top 3): data residency per region, predictable tail latency (p99 SLO), and private dedicated pools. Those correlate to premium contracts.

joel: Important: include a compatibility matrix for models and quantization that shows which families can run in a given lane. This will affect pricing and packaging.

nick: Proposed canary plan: 7-day canary, 5-10% traffic, two region pairs, must hit perf regressions <4% p95 and no KV divergence.

sana: Example launch criteria draft:
- Capacity commit confirmed (ops & sales)
- Canary (>=7d) across 2 regions with synthetic and live traffic
- Acceptance tests: KV cache parity, latency SLOs, error-rate <0.5%
- Runbook & rollback playbook documented and exercised

meera: Operational playbook items: evacuation script, tenant quarantine CLI, throttles, and alert run handlers. Also need tagged telemetry for "policy_decision" events.

keiko: Suggested rollback SLI: if error rate increased >1% for 10m on canary, auto-fallback to global routing for affected tenants.

joel: Example policy payload (proto):
```
{
  "policy_name":"regional_preference",
  "preferences":{
    "primary_region":"eu-west1",
    "fallback_policy":"global_fallback",
    "constraints": ["resident_data_only"],
    "eviction":{ "soft_threshold":0.85, "hard_threshold":0.95 }
  }
}
```

eva: Pricing note: isolation lanes will need a per-tenant uplift. Redwood Optimize should estimate uplift by model family and tail-latency budget.

nick: Tech constraints: some accelerated kernels don't support specific quantized formats. We need a short spike (10 working days) to produce: compatibility matrix + cost uplift estimates + test harness for cross-region KV checks.

sana: I'll own the spike and produce a one-pager + acceptance matrix. Delivery target: 10 working days.

ci-bot: CI: spike branch created: feature/routing-lanes-spike by sana. Auto-run: perf-harness on eu/us pairs.

meera: Also capture customer impact stories in the spec: 1) enterprise legal/regulatory residency, 2) platform team wanting SLA for latency-sensitive features, 3) high-volume customers needing deterministic throughput.

keiko: Ops asks to be explicit about monitoring events: policy_decision.{tenant,policy_id,decision}, route_fallback.{tenant,reason}, kv_reconcile.{tenant,status}.

joel: OK. Next steps: sana owns one-pager + canary plan + telemetry list. Nick to draft pricing uplift model assumptions with finance. Meera to sketch runbook templates. We'll review next Wed.

sana: Understood. I'll post the draft in #product by Tue EOD.

nick: I'll sync with finance & Redwood Optimize folks today.

ci-bot: Calendar: product review scheduled Wed 15:00 UTC.

joel: Thanks all. This should be distinct from the infra-only routing docs 1 want the product-facing acceptance criteria to be obvious for sales and customers. :white_check_mark:
